correctness.rationale: Four independently placed cuts parametrize all words, and exactly count each abc subsequence by a hinge overlap. The symmetrized hinge expression reduces to a parity-respecting integer-grid lemma whose monotone strip path proves full interval support. The h=0 case is checked separately. Reversal and explicit finite sums give the global polynomial. Checker.py directly tests 93,024 words and 5,456 complete slices, plus 2,500 seeded larger slices; no extrapolation from finite tests is used.

value.rationale: This is a natural exact image-size and feasibility problem for the Parikh matrix of a fixed-content word, motivated by indistinguishability under scattered-subword measurements. The cubic cardinality quantifies a strong compression from quartically many words; the full image includes a sharp parity-obstruction hyperslice invisible to coarse asymptotic bounds. The result is an all-parameter classification with direct potential use in fixed-content ambiguity studies, not an arbitrary single computation.
